name: Old Quarter
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: The Old Quarter is the tight grid of lanes north of Hoan Kiem Lake. Streets still carry traces of the old guild trades. It is the easiest place to stay on a first night and the easiest place to overpay for a meal.
timeNeeded: Half a day to a full day
getThere: Walk north from Hoan Kiem Lake
seoTitle: Hanoi Old Quarter — a walking guide
seoDescription: What the Hanoi Old Quarter is, how to walk it, and where to sleep if you want to be in the middle of it.
intro: The Old Quarter sits on land that was once a cluster of artisan streets outside the citadel. Shop signs still hint at silver, silk, and herbal medicine, even where the ground floors now sell luggage and cafe seats.
Walk it in the morning, before the pavements are fully claimed by motorbikes and stools. Use the timed walk if you want a route instead of a wander.
gettingAround: Arrive on foot from the lake. The lanes are short and the map looks simpler than the traffic. A bicycle is possible and often slower than walking.

stayAreas.name: Near the lake end
stayAreas.summary: Shorter walks to Hoan Kiem and an easier exit by car.

stayAreas.name: Deeper lanes
stayAreas.summary: More local street life and more night noise.

eat: Bun cha, pho, and egg coffee are all within a few blocks. Choose a place with a written price and a crowd of residents, not only visitors.
interestsBody: The quarter is the food and walking district of Hanoi. It is not the place for quiet temples; those sit a short ride away.

interestGroups.title: Walking the lanes
interestGroups.summary: Walk it in the morning, before the pavements are fully claimed.

cards.title: Bach Ma Temple
cards.summary: A small neighborhood temple on Hang Buom, easy to include in a walk.

cards.title: Dong Xuan Market
cards.summary: The quarter’s main covered market, useful for a look at wholesale goods more than for souvenirs.

faqs.q: Is the Old Quarter safe at night?
faqs.a: The lanes stay busy into the evening. Watch your bag in crowds and cross as the locals do, at a steady pace.
